questions.question: India has celebrated 76th Independence day in which year ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2022.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India celebrated its **76th Independence Day** in the year 2022.
 
• India gained independence from British rule on **August 15, 1947,** and since then, every year, India celebrates its** Independence Day **on the same date.
 
• As of now, India has celebrated **75 Independence Day** on** August 15, 2021.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India's Independence Day **is a national holiday celebrated with** great enthusiasm and patriotic fervor **throughout the country.
 
• The main celebration takes place in the **national capital, New Delhi,** where the Prime Minister of India** hoists the national flag **and delivers a speech from the ramparts of the historic Red Fort.
 
• Apart from the national capital, Independence Day is celebrated in all the states and union territories of India with **flag hoisting, parades, cultural programs, and other events.**
 
• The celebration of Independence Day is a reminder of **India's struggle for freedom **and the sacrifices made by the** freedom fighters** to make India an independent and sovereign nation.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution enshrines the right against exploitation ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 23 and 24.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **right against exploitation** is enshrined in **Article 23 and 24 **of the Indian constitution.
 
• **Article 23** prohibits trafficking of **human beings and forced labor,** while **Article 24** prohibits the employment of children below the age of **14 years** in hazardous industries.
 
• These articles are a part of the **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed to every citizen of India.
 
• The right against exploitation is crucial in ensuring the** protection of vulnerable sections** of the **society,** especially women and children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Informations__**

 
• Article 27 and 28 deal with the freedom to practice and propagate religion.
 
• Article 21 enshrines the right to life and personal liberty.
 
• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.

questions.question: ___________ refers to a method adopted by the Central Bank to persuade or convince the commercial banks to advance credit in the economic interest of the country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Moral Suasion.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Moral suasion is a method adopted by the Central Bank to persuade or convince the commercial banks to advance credit in the economic interest of the country. 
 
• It is a non-quantitative method of credit control as it does not involve any direct changes in the interest rates or reserve requirements.
 
• The Central Bank uses its influence and credibility to persuade the commercial banks to follow certain guidelines or policies that are deemed necessary for the economic growth and stability of the country.
 
• Moral suasion can be effective in situations where the Central Bank has a good reputation and credibility among the commercial banks and the public.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) is a borrowing window for the banks to borrow funds from the Central Bank in case of emergency or shortage of liquidity.
 
 
• It is a quantitative method of credit control.
 
 
 
• Credit rationing is a method of credit control where the Central Bank restricts the availability of credit to certain sectors or borrowers to control inflation or prevent speculative activities.
 
• Margin requirements refer to the minimum amount of collateral or margin that a borrower has to maintain for a loan or investment.

questions.question: Negative ions that consist of a single atom are named by adding the suffix ___________ to the stem of the name of the element.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-ide.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The suffix "-ide" is added to the stem of the name of the element to form the name of negative ions consisting of a single atom.
 
• For example, chlorine forms chloride ion (Cl-) and oxygen forms oxide ion (O2-).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The suffix "-ous" is used for naming cations with lower charge, such as Cu+ (cuprous ion).
 
• The suffix "-ic" is used for cations with higher charge, such as Cu2+ (cupric ion).
 
• The suffix "-onium" is used for naming positively charged ions composed of two or more atoms, such as ammonium ion (NH4+).
 
• The suffix "-ate" is used for naming oxyanions with higher oxidation state, such as sulfate ion (SO42-), while the suffix "-ite" is used for oxyanions with lower oxidation state, such as sulfite ion (SO32-).

questions.question: Four ashrams were recognised by Brahmins around the time when Jainism and Buddhism were becoming popular. Which of the following was NOT a recognised ashrama?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parmarth.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Parmarth was **not** a recognised ashrama.
 
• The four recognised ashramas were **Grihastha, Vanaprastha, Brahmacharya, and Sannyasa.**
 
• These ashramas were recognised by Brahmins as stages of life that an individual would pass through in order to attain spiritual growth and enlightenment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Grihastha was the householder stage, where an individual would get married and fulfill their worldly duties.
 
• Vanaprastha was the retirement stage, where an individual would withdraw from worldly affairs and focus on spiritual pursuits.
 
• Brahmacharya was the student stage, where an individual would study under a guru and learn the scriptures.
 
• Sannyasa was the renunciate stage, where an individual would renounce all worldly possessions and dedicate themselves completely to spiritual pursuits.

questions.question: Cytology is the study of ___________.

__
 
• Cytology is the branch of biology that deals with the study of cells and their structure, functions, and interactions with other cells.
 
• It involves the examination of cells under the microscope to understand their morphology, physiology, and biochemistry.
 
• Cytology is important in fields such as genetics, pathology, and cancer research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroplasts** are organelles found in** plant cells** that are responsible for **photosynthesis.**
 
• **Tissues **are groups of cells that perform a** specific function** in an organism.
 
• **Genes **are the **basic units of heredity** that carry information for the development and **function of cells and organisms. **

questions.question: Which among the following is an example of Angiosperm in Plant Kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tomato.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Angiosperms** are flowering plants that **produce seeds** enclosed within an ovary.
 
• The **tomato plant** is an example of an angiosperm.
 
• **Chara** is a** genus of green algae **that belongs to the division** Charophyta**. It is not an angiosperm.
 
• **Pinus** is a **genus of gymnosperms**, which are plants that produce seeds that are not enclosed within an ovary.
 
• They are commonly known as** conifers **and include trees such as **pines, spruces, and firs.**
 
• **Funaria **is a** genus of mosses** that belongs to the division** Bryophyta.**
 
• **Mosses** are **non-vascular plants** that do not produce seeds or flowers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Angiosperms make up the largest group of plants on Earth, with over 300,000 species.
 
• They are divided into two main groups: monocotyledons (monocots) and dicotyledons (dicots), based on the number of seed leaves (cotyledons) they produce.
 
• Gymnosperms include around 1,000 species and are mostly trees or shrubs. 
 
• Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts, and hornworts) are small, non-vascular plants that play an important role in ecosystem processes such as carbon cycling and soil formation.

questions.question: The founder of Brahmo Sabha was ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** founder of Brahmo Sabha** was **Raja Ram Mohan Roy,** who was a social reformer and a pioneer of modern Indian Renaissance.
 
• **He established the** **Brahmo Sabha in 1828 in Kolkata** **with the aim of promoting** **monotheism and reforming Hindu society.**
 
• The Brahmo Sabha later evolved into the Brahmo Samaj, which became a major **socio-religious movement in India.**
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy was also a champion of **women's rights and education**, and played a key role in the **abolition of Sati **and the introduction of **English education** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keshab Chandra Sen** was a prominent leader of the **Brahmo Samaj** in the later years, and played a key role in its** expansion and modernization.**
 
• **Radhakanta Deb **was a prominent figure in the early years of the Brahmo Sabha, and was one of the** first members of the organization.**
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore** was a **renowned poet, writer, and philosopher** who was associated with the Brahmo Samaj, but he was not its founder.
 
• He was the first Asian to win the** Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.**

questions.question: The Himalayan mountain range is a type of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fold mountains.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Himalayan mountain range is a type of fold mountains.**
 
• Fold mountains are formed when two tectonic plates collide, and the crust is pushed upwards, forming folds or wrinkles.
 
• **The Himalayan mountain range was formed due to the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates**.
 
• The Himalayas are the highest mountain range in the world, with several peaks above 8000 meters.
 
• This is because of the intense folding and upliftment of rocks that occurred during the collision of the two plates.
 
• The Himalayas are still rising at a rate of about 5 mm per year due to the ongoing collision of the plates.
 
• This also makes the region prone to earthquakes and landslides.
 
• **Other examples of fold mountains include the Andes in South America, the Alps in Europe, and the Rockies in North America.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Residual mountains are formed due to erosion of existing mountains.
 
 
• They are usually lower in height and have a more rounded appearance.
 
• An example of residual mountains is the Appalachian Mountains in North America.
 
 
 
• Block mountains are formed due to the cracking and upliftment of the earth's crust.
 
 
• **They have steep slopes on one side and gentler slopes on the other.**
 
• **An example of block mountains is the Sierra Nevada range in California.**
 
 
 
• Accumulated mountains are formed due to the accumulation of volcanic material over time.
 
 
• They are usually conical in shape and have a crater at the top.
 
• **An example of accumulated mountains is Mount Fuji in Japan.**

questions.question: The Amaravati School of art was developed under the patronage of ___________.

The correct answer is __**1907.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The split in **Indian National Congress** occurred in **1907.**
 
• **The split was a result of ideological differences between the moderates and the extremists.**
 
• The moderates believed in the** peaceful and gradual approach** towards gaining independence from the British rule.
 
• The extremists, on the other hand, believed in a more** **radical approach and were willing to use violence if necessary.
 
• The split led to the formation of two factions within the Congress -** the Garam Dal (Extremist faction) and the Naram Dal (Moderate faction)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The year **1905 **is significant in the history of Indian National Congress as it was the year when the** partition of Bengal **was announced by **Lord Curzon**, which led to widespread protests and agitation across the country.
